bio: Bill Ackman founded Pershing Square Capital Management in 2004 after his first fund, Gotham Partners, wound down following a series of high-profile but ultimately unsuccessful activist campaigns. Born in 1966 and raised in Chappaqua, New York, Ackman graduated from Harvard College magna cum laude in 1988 and earned his MBA from Harvard Business School in 1992. He is known as one of the most vocal and media-savvy investors in the world, regularly publishing detailed investment theses and engaging publicly in debates about his positions.

Pershing Square operates with an unusually concentrated portfolio — typically holding fewer than 15 positions — and takes large, often controlling stakes in publicly traded companies with the goal of influencing management or strategy. The fund has delivered exceptional long-term returns, including the legendary COVID hedge in early 2020 that turned a $27M premium into $2.6B in profit over a matter of weeks. Ackman launched Pershing Square USA (PSUS) in 2024 as a closed-end fund, giving retail investors direct access to his strategy.
philosophy_quote: We look for simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative businesses with dominant market positions, where we can invest at a discount to intrinsic value and where we can be an active catalyst for change.

notable_trades.title: COVID Hedge (2020)
notable_trades.desc: Turned a $27M credit default swap position into $2.6B in roughly three weeks as markets collapsed. One of the greatest single trades in hedge fund history.

notable_trades.title: General Growth Properties (2009)
notable_trades.desc: Bought a significant stake in GGP while it was in bankruptcy. The company emerged and Pershing made over $1.6B on the trade.

notable_trades.title: Herbalife Short (2012–2018)
notable_trades.desc: A very public $1B short bet that Herbalife was a pyramid scheme. The position ultimately cost Pershing around $1B after Herbalife survived.

notable_trades.title: Valeant Pharmaceuticals (2015–2017)
notable_trades.desc: A concentrated long position that turned catastrophic after accounting irregularities and drug pricing controversies. Losses of roughly $4B.

notable_trades.title: Brookfield Corp (BN)
notable_trades.desc: One of Pershing's largest current positions. Ackman has spoken positively about Brookfield's long-term compounding potential.

notable_trades.title: Alphabet / Nike
notable_trades.desc: Pershing initiated positions in both Google parent Alphabet and Nike in 2023, viewing them as dominant franchises trading below intrinsic value.

bio: Warren Buffett is widely regarded as the greatest investor of all time. Born in 1930 in Omaha, Nebraska, he displayed a talent for business and investing from childhood, filing his first tax return at age 13. He studied under Benjamin Graham at Columbia Business School, absorbing the principles of value investing that would define his career. He took control of Berkshire Hathaway in 1965 — then a failing textile company — and transformed it into one of the world's largest conglomerates with a market capitalization exceeding $1 trillion.

Berkshire's investment philosophy centers on buying wonderful businesses at fair prices and holding them forever. Buffett is famous for his patience, his disdain for excessive fees and complexity, and his annual shareholder letters, which have become required reading for investors worldwide. His long-time partner Charlie Munger, who passed away in 2023, was instrumental in shifting Buffett's approach from pure Graham-style bargain hunting toward quality businesses with durable competitive advantages.
philosophy_quote: It is far better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price.

notable_trades.title: Coca-Cola (1988)
notable_trades.desc: Began buying Coke after the 1987 crash. The position has returned many multiples and Berkshire still holds it today, collecting hundreds of millions in annual dividends.

notable_trades.title: American Express (1960s)
notable_trades.desc: Bought a massive stake during the Salad Oil Scandal when AmEx was briefly in crisis. One of the first demonstrations of Buffett's conviction-based approach.

notable_trades.title: Apple (2016–present)
notable_trades.desc: Began buying Apple in 2016 and built it into Berkshire's largest position at peak. Called it 'probably the best business I know in the world.'

notable_trades.title: Dexter Shoe (1993)
notable_trades.desc: Paid $433M in Berkshire stock for a shoe company that was quickly wiped out by foreign competition. Called it his worst deal ever.

notable_trades.title: Bank of America
notable_trades.desc: A massive financial sector bet reflecting Buffett's long-held conviction in US banking and consumer finance over the long term.

notable_trades.title: Occidental Petroleum
notable_trades.desc: Berkshire has aggressively accumulated OXY shares and warrants, making it a major energy sector bet at attractive valuations.

bio: Greg Abel became CEO of Berkshire Hathaway on January 1, 2026, succeeding Warren Buffett who had led the company for over 60 years. Born in Edmonton, Alberta in 1962, Abel studied accounting at the University of Alberta before beginning a career in the energy sector. He joined MidAmerican Energy in 1992 and rose to become its CEO, overseeing its transformation into one of the largest utility holding companies in the United States. Berkshire Hathaway acquired a controlling stake in MidAmerican in 1999, bringing Abel into the Berkshire orbit.

Abel was named Vice Chairman of Berkshire's non-insurance operations in 2018, and Buffett publicly identified him as his chosen successor in 2021. He is known as an extraordinarily disciplined operator — a hands-on executive who personally negotiates deals, reviews contracts, and travels constantly to the businesses he oversees. His style is quieter and more internally focused than Buffett's, and he has signaled continuity with Berkshire's core philosophy: patient capital allocation, decentralized management, permanent ownership of great businesses, and extreme conservatism on financial risk.
philosophy_quote: Berkshire's culture is its competitive advantage. We will continue to look for great businesses run by great people, hold them for the long term, and never put the company in a position where it has to do something it doesn't want to do.

notable_trades.title: MidAmerican Energy buildout
notable_trades.desc: Led MidAmerican's transformation from a regional utility into a major renewable energy platform, investing billions in wind and solar generation ahead of the sector.

notable_trades.title: BHE renewable expansion
notable_trades.desc: Under Abel, Berkshire Hathaway Energy became one of the largest owners of wind and solar generation capacity in the US, a long-term positioning play.

notable_trades.title: Berkshire non-insurance operations
notable_trades.desc: Oversaw a portfolio of businesses generating tens of billions in annual revenue, from BNSF railroad to See's Candies to Dairy Queen, maintaining Berkshire's decentralized culture.

notable_trades.title: Inheriting Buffett's portfolio
notable_trades.desc: As CEO, Abel now oversees Berkshire's massive public equity portfolio including Apple, Bank of America, Coca-Cola, and Occidental Petroleum, built almost entirely by Buffett.

notable_trades.title: Capital allocation decisions
notable_trades.desc: Abel faces the central question of what to do with Berkshire's enormous cash pile, and how to deploy capital at scale in a market where truly great businesses rarely come cheap.

bio: Charlie Munger was the Vice Chairman of Berkshire Hathaway and Warren Buffett's closest partner for over 45 years, until his passing on November 28, 2023 at the age of 99. Born in Omaha, Nebraska in 1924, Munger studied mathematics at the University of Michigan before serving in World War II as a meteorologist. He earned his law degree from Harvard Law School in 1948 without ever completing an undergraduate degree, going on to practice law in Los Angeles before partnering with Buffett. It was Munger who persuaded Buffett to evolve beyond Benjamin Graham's strict cigar-butt bargain hunting and instead pay fair prices for truly great businesses — a shift that defined Berkshire's transformation into one of the greatest wealth creation stories in history.

Alongside Berkshire, Munger served as Chairman of Daily Journal Corporation from 1977 until his death, using it as a vehicle for his own independent investment thinking in later life. Under his stewardship, Daily Journal's investment portfolio — small relative to Berkshire but closely watched by value investors worldwide — held concentrated positions including a large stake in Alibaba that he initiated in his 90s, demonstrating conviction and intellectual independence until the very end. Daily Journal is now led by CEO Rick Guerin's successor Gary Salzman, with the board continuing to steward the company's legal publishing and software businesses. Munger's annual remarks at the Daily Journal shareholder meeting in Los Angeles, delivered without notes into his late 90s, became required viewing for serious students of investing and business.
philosophy_quote: It's not supposed to be easy. Anyone who finds it easy is stupid. It requires a broad understanding of the nature of things and the ability to apply that understanding in a rational way.

notable_trades.title: Berkshire partnership (1978–2023)
notable_trades.desc: As Vice Chairman alongside Buffett, helped guide Berkshire from a struggling textile company into a $700B+ conglomerate, one of the greatest wealth creation stories in history.

notable_trades.title: Blue Chip Stamps / See's Candies
notable_trades.desc: Munger was instrumental in the 1972 acquisition of See's Candies for $25M — a business that has since generated over $2B in cumulative pre-tax earnings and taught Buffett the power of brand and pricing.

notable_trades.title: Wesco Financial Corporation
notable_trades.desc: Munger ran Wesco Financial as Chairman from 1984 to 2011, building it into a diversified holding company before merging it fully into Berkshire Hathaway.

notable_trades.title: Daily Journal Corporation
notable_trades.desc: As Chairman of Daily Journal Corp, steered its investment portfolio into concentrated positions including a large Alibaba stake, demonstrating his independent conviction in later life.

notable_trades.title: Costco board (1997–2021)
notable_trades.desc: A longtime Costco board member, Munger was one of the earliest and most vocal advocates for the warehouse club model as a durable, customer-obsessed business.

bio: Michael Burry is one of the most unconventional investors alive. A trained physician who taught himself to invest while completing his medical residency, Burry founded Scion Capital in 2000 and quickly attracted attention for his ability to identify deeply undervalued stocks through exhaustive bottom-up research. His early returns were extraordinary, beating the market significantly in the years immediately following the dot-com bust.

Burry became globally famous for being one of the first investors to recognize the housing bubble and bet against it via credit default swaps on mortgage-backed securities — a trade that generated over $700M in profits for his investors and $100M personally, immortalized in Michael Lewis's book and later film 'The Big Short.' He closed Scion Capital in 2008, retreated from public life, and re-emerged in 2013 with the family office Scion Asset Management. He is now known for concentrated, high-conviction positions and frequent macro warnings on social media.
philosophy_quote: My strategy isn't very complex. I try to buy shares of unpopular companies when they look like road kill, and sell them when they've been rehabilitated.

notable_trades.title: The Big Short (2005–2007)
notable_trades.desc: Identified the US housing bubble and bought credit default swaps on subprime mortgage bonds. Generated $700M+ for investors when the market collapsed in 2007–2008.

notable_trades.title: GameStop (pre-2021)
notable_trades.desc: Was an early GameStop investor before the meme stock phenomenon, recognizing the company's hidden real estate value and activist potential.

notable_trades.title: Geo Group short (2019)
notable_trades.desc: Took a short position on private prison operator GEO Group expecting regulatory headwinds. The position moved against him significantly.

notable_trades.title: Various deep value plays
notable_trades.desc: Scion's portfolio rotates through deeply discounted small and mid-cap companies, often in out-of-favor sectors trading well below book value.

notable_trades.title: China tech / JD.com
notable_trades.desc: Has taken positions in beaten-down Chinese internet companies, betting on valuation reversion despite geopolitical risk.

bio: Stanley Druckenmiller is considered by many professional investors to be the greatest macro trader of all time. He managed Duquesne Capital from 1981 until converting it to a family office in 2010, achieving an extraordinary 30-year track record with no down years. From 1988 to 2000, he served as the lead portfolio manager for George Soros's Quantum Fund, where he executed the legendary 1992 trade that 'broke the Bank of England' by shorting the British pound — generating $1B in profit in a single day.

Druckenmiller's approach combines top-down macro analysis with bottom-up stock picking. He is known for his ability to identify major economic turning points early, concentrate heavily when he has conviction, and adapt quickly when wrong. Unlike most macro managers, he also invests significantly in individual equities. He has been an outspoken critic of excessive US government spending and a frequent commentator on monetary policy and market structure.
philosophy_quote: The way to build superior long-term returns is through preservation of capital and home runs. You can be wrong 30% of the time and still make a fortune if you cut losses and let winners run.

notable_trades.title: Breaking the Bank of England (1992)
notable_trades.desc: Working with George Soros, shorted the British pound ahead of the UK's forced exit from the European Exchange Rate Mechanism. Made $1B in a single day.

notable_trades.title: Dot-com short (2000)
notable_trades.desc: Shorted technology stocks at the peak of the dot-com bubble, though he initially lost money going long before switching to a massive short position.

notable_trades.title: Post-GFC recovery (2009)
notable_trades.desc: Correctly called the market bottom in early 2009 and positioned aggressively in equities as other macro players remained bearish.

notable_trades.title: Dot-com long (early 2000)
notable_trades.desc: Initially went long technology stocks near the peak, losing $3B before reversing and going short. A rare and costly mistake.

notable_trades.title: AI infrastructure plays
notable_trades.desc: Has been bullish on companies benefiting from AI infrastructure buildout, including semiconductor and data center names.

bio: David Tepper founded Appaloosa Management in 1993 after being passed over for a partnership at Goldman Sachs, where he had been head of high-yield trading. He built Appaloosa into one of the most successful hedge funds in history, with a specialty in distressed debt and event-driven situations. The fund is known for extraordinary performance in crisis periods, when Tepper's ability to assess credit risk and corporate recovery scenarios gives him a decisive edge.

Tepper is perhaps best known for his prescient call in 2009 that the US government would not allow major banks to fail, leading to a massive long position in financial stocks that returned over $7B — reportedly the largest single-year hedge fund gain in history at the time. He converted Appaloosa to a family office in 2019, returning outside capital. He also owns the Carolina Panthers NFL franchise, purchased in 2018 for $2.275B.
philosophy_quote: The key is to wait. Sometimes the hardest thing to do is to do nothing. The big money is made in the markets when you have a clear thesis and everything lines up.

notable_trades.title: Bank stocks recovery (2009)
notable_trades.desc: Bet heavily that the US government would not allow major banks to fail. The trade returned over $7B — one of the largest single-year gains in hedge fund history.

notable_trades.title: Distressed debt cycles
notable_trades.desc: Appaloosa has repeatedly made fortunes buying distressed corporate debt in crises, including the 2002 telecom bust and 2008 financial crisis.

notable_trades.title: Marconi (2002)
notable_trades.desc: Bought the distressed debt of UK telecom company Marconi and made enormous returns as the company restructured.

notable_trades.title: Various macro shorts
notable_trades.desc: Tepper has occasionally lost money on macro positions, particularly when betting against central bank intervention proved premature.

notable_trades.title: Large-cap tech
notable_trades.desc: Appaloosa's current public equity portfolio is concentrated in mega-cap technology companies alongside select financials.

bio: Seth Klarman is one of the most respected and private figures in the investment world. He founded Baupost Group in 1982 with just $27M in capital from Harvard's endowment and four families, and has grown it into one of the largest hedge funds in the world. Unlike most hedge fund managers, Klarman frequently holds significant cash — sometimes 30–50% of the portfolio — waiting for compelling opportunities rather than forcing capital to work. Baupost has historically held illiquid and complex assets alongside public equities.

Klarman is the author of 'Margin of Safety,' a 1991 book on value investing that is so sought after it sells for over $1,000 on the secondary market. The book articulates his core philosophy: obsessive focus on downside risk, insistence on a large margin of safety between price and intrinsic value, and the patience to wait years for opportunities. He is deeply skeptical of market efficiency and the financial establishment, and has been a consistent voice warning about the risks of central bank intervention and excessive leverage.
philosophy_quote: The single greatest edge an investor can have is a long-term orientation. Most of Wall Street is focused on this quarter. If you focus on three to five years, you have very little competition.

notable_trades.title: Post-GFC distressed assets
notable_trades.desc: Baupost aggressively bought distressed mortgage securities and corporate debt after 2008, generating substantial returns as markets recovered.

notable_trades.title: Real estate debt (various)
notable_trades.desc: Has repeatedly made large returns buying real estate-related debt at distressed prices during property market downturns.

notable_trades.title: Theravance Biopharma
notable_trades.desc: A complex spinoff and biotech restructuring situation that played out to Baupost's benefit over several years.

notable_trades.title: Energy sector (2014–2016)
notable_trades.desc: Like many value investors, Baupost bought energy names during the oil price collapse that proved to be value traps as prices fell further.

notable_trades.title: Healthcare / biotech
notable_trades.desc: Baupost has maintained significant exposure to healthcare and biotech, areas where complexity creates mispricing opportunities.

bio: Daniel Loeb founded Third Point LLC in 1995 with $3.3M in seed capital, including money from family and friends, and has grown it into one of the leading activist hedge funds. Third Point is known for its sharply worded shareholder letters, often addressed to underperforming management teams, which have become some of the most widely read documents on Wall Street. Loeb has targeted companies ranging from Yahoo and Sotheby's to Sony and Nestlé, pushing for management changes, divestitures, and strategic reviews.

Beyond activism, Third Point runs a diverse book spanning equities, credit, structured products, and private investments. Loeb is also a significant art collector and philanthropist, funding education reform initiatives in New York. He has evolved as an investor over his career — early in Third Point's history the fund focused heavily on distressed credit, while today it blends fundamental long/short equity with activist campaigns and macro overlays.
philosophy_quote: We want to own great businesses, managed by great people, at prices that make sense. When management disappoints, we believe shareholders have both the right and the responsibility to demand change.

notable_trades.title: Yahoo / Marissa Mayer campaign (2012)
notable_trades.desc: Exposed resume fabrications of Yahoo CEO Scott Thompson, forcing his resignation and eventually gaining board seats. Third Point made substantial gains on Yahoo's Alibaba stake.

notable_trades.title: Sotheby's (2013–2014)
notable_trades.desc: Pushed for management changes and capital return at the auction house. Gained board representation and profited handsomely.

notable_trades.title: Sony campaign (2013)
notable_trades.desc: Pushed Sony to spin off its entertainment division. Though the spinoff didn't happen, the campaign drew attention to undervalued assets.

notable_trades.title: Nestlé long (2017–2019)
notable_trades.desc: Took a large stake and pushed for aggressive restructuring. The campaign had limited impact on Nestlé's entrenched management culture.

notable_trades.title: Technology & healthcare
notable_trades.desc: Third Point's current equity book is concentrated in technology and healthcare, with a mix of long-term compounders and event-driven situations.

bio: David Einhorn founded Greenlight Capital in 1996 at age 27 with $900,000 from family and friends. He built it into a premier long/short equity fund over the next two decades, known especially for his rigorous short selling research and public presentations at investment conferences. Einhorn became famous for his prescient short of Lehman Brothers in 2007 — years before its collapse — and for a series of other famous shorts including Allied Capital and Green Mountain Coffee Roasters.

Greenlight experienced a difficult stretch from 2014 to 2020 as its short book struggled in a relentlessly rising market, particularly against technology stocks. Einhorn restructured the fund and rebranded it as DME Capital Management. He has remained a vocal critic of 'bubble' market conditions and passive investing. Outside of markets, he is an accomplished poker player, finishing 18th in the 2012 World Series of Poker Main Event and donating his winnings to charity.
philosophy_quote: We try to find situations where we have a differentiated view from the consensus, backed by thorough research, and where the market price doesn't reflect the reality we see.

notable_trades.title: Lehman Brothers short (2007–2008)
notable_trades.desc: Publicly presented his short thesis on Lehman at a conference in 2007, over a year before its collapse. One of the most famous calls in hedge fund history.

notable_trades.title: Allied Capital short (2002–2007)
notable_trades.desc: Spent years publicly arguing Allied Capital was mismarking its loan portfolio. Eventually proven right after a regulatory investigation.

notable_trades.title: Apple long (2016)
notable_trades.desc: Campaigned for Apple to issue preferred stock and return more cash. Made significant gains as the position appreciated.

notable_trades.title: Tesla short (2014–2019)
notable_trades.desc: Held a short position in Tesla through a painful multiyear period as the stock surged. Cost Greenlight hundreds of millions.

notable_trades.title: Value / energy plays
notable_trades.desc: DME's current book focuses on deeply discounted value stocks and select energy names Einhorn views as misunderstood by the market.

bio: Peter Thiel is one of the most influential technology investors and thinkers of his generation. Co-founder of PayPal, Palantir Technologies, and the first outside investor in Facebook, Thiel's public market vehicle Thiel Macro manages a portion of his considerable fortune. His investing philosophy is deeply shaped by his contrarian worldview: he looks for companies that have built monopoly-like positions in markets others have overlooked, and macro positions that reflect his often heterodox views on government, technology, and society.

Thiel is the author of 'Zero to One,' a book on startups and innovation that has become required reading in Silicon Valley. He is a vocal critic of higher education, offering the Thiel Fellowship to pay promising young people to skip college and start companies instead. His public market portfolio, while smaller than his private investments, tends to reflect concentrated bets in technology and defense-adjacent companies, as well as macro positions that often include gold and inflation hedges.
philosophy_quote: Competition is for losers. If you want to create and capture lasting value, look to build a monopoly. In the market for innovation, the best companies create entirely new categories.

notable_trades.title: Facebook seed investment (2004)
notable_trades.desc: Invested $500,000 for roughly 10% of Facebook in its earliest days. Sold most of his stake in 2012 for over $1B, one of the greatest VC returns ever.

notable_trades.title: PayPal (1998–2002)
notable_trades.desc: Co-founded PayPal and sold it to eBay for $1.5B in 2002, seeding the so-called 'PayPal Mafia' of serial entrepreneurs and investors.

notable_trades.title: Palantir (2003–present)
notable_trades.desc: Co-founded the data analytics firm and remains a significant shareholder. Palantir went public in 2020 and has grown substantially.

notable_trades.title: Defense tech / AI
notable_trades.desc: Thiel Macro's public positions reflect conviction in defense technology companies, AI infrastructure, and select technology platforms.

notable_trades.title: Gold / inflation hedges
notable_trades.desc: Known for holding gold and other inflation-sensitive assets as a hedge against what Thiel sees as inevitable monetary debasement.

bio: Sir Christopher Hohn is the founder of TCI Fund Management, one of the highest-returning hedge funds in the world over the past two decades. Born in Surrey, England, Hohn studied at Southampton University before earning his MBA from Harvard Business School. He founded TCI in 2003 after working at Perry Capital, and structured it with a charitable component — a significant portion of TCI's profits flow to the Children's Investment Fund Foundation (CIFF), which has become one of the largest philanthropic organizations in the UK.

TCI's strategy is built on extreme concentration — typically holding fewer than 15 positions — with very long holding periods and active engagement with management teams. Hohn is known for being both a patient long-term owner and a fierce activist when companies fail to meet expectations. He was a key figure in the hostile takeover bid for the London Stock Exchange in 2004 and has waged public campaigns against railroad companies, airlines, and European banks. He has also become a leading voice on climate risk in corporate governance.
philosophy_quote: We invest in companies with strong competitive positions, high returns on capital, and management teams that allocate capital well. Then we hold them for years and let compounding do the work.

notable_trades.title: ABN AMRO campaign (2007)
notable_trades.desc: TCI's letter to ABN AMRO's board demanding a breakup helped trigger a bidding war that valued the bank at €71B, generating substantial returns.

notable_trades.title: Railroad compounders
notable_trades.desc: TCI has made enormous returns holding major North American railroad companies for extended periods, benefiting from pricing power and volume growth.

notable_trades.title: Visa / Mastercard
notable_trades.desc: Long-term positions in payment network duopolists have been core to TCI's returns, with near-monopoly economics and decades-long growth runways.

notable_trades.title: Various airline positions
notable_trades.desc: TCI's 2019 position in airlines preceded the COVID pandemic, which devastated the sector. Hohn was vocal about management's poor capital allocation.

notable_trades.title: Technology mega-caps
notable_trades.desc: TCI's concentrated portfolio includes major technology platforms and financial infrastructure companies held for multi-year periods.

bio: Leon Cooperman grew up in the South Bronx and put himself through Columbia University, where he later earned his MBA. He spent 25 years at Goldman Sachs, becoming head of equity research and then running Goldman Sachs Asset Management, before leaving in 1991 to found Omega Advisors. His fund became one of the most respected on Wall Street over the following decades, known for rigorous fundamental analysis and a growth-at-a-reasonable-price philosophy.

Cooperman converted Omega to a family office in 2018 after settling insider trading charges with the SEC — charges he contested publicly and vigorously. He is known as one of Wall Street's most outspoken personalities, a frequent CNBC commentator, and a vocal critic of wealth taxes. He signed the Giving Pledge, committing to donate the majority of his wealth to charity. He continues to manage his personal capital with the same disciplined approach he applied at Omega.
philosophy_quote: I am a bottom-up stock picker. I look for companies with strong earnings momentum, good management, and reasonable valuations. The macro environment matters, but it doesn't drive individual security selection.

notable_trades.title: Financial crisis recovery (2009)
notable_trades.desc: Aggressively bought discounted financials and industrials at the market bottom, generating strong returns as the economy recovered.

notable_trades.title: Energy stocks (various cycles)
notable_trades.desc: Cooperman has repeatedly made money in energy stocks, buying when sector sentiment is poor and valuations are depressed.

notable_trades.title: Alphabet / Google (long-term)
notable_trades.desc: Has been a long-term holder of Alphabet, viewing it as a dominant business trading at reasonable valuations relative to growth.

notable_trades.title: Atlas Resource Partners
notable_trades.desc: A natural gas MLP position that went poorly as energy prices collapsed and the company faced financial difficulties.

notable_trades.title: Diversified value / income
notable_trades.desc: Cooperman's family office holds a diversified mix of value-oriented equities and income-generating positions across sectors.

bio: Carl Icahn is the original corporate raider — the prototype for activist investing before the term was invented. Born in Queens, New York in 1936, he studied philosophy at Princeton and briefly attended NYU medical school before deciding Wall Street was more interesting. He began his career as a stockbroker and options trader, then pivoted to buying large stakes in underperforming companies and aggressively demanding change. In the 1980s he was part of a wave of corporate raiders that transformed American corporate governance.

Icahn has targeted dozens of major corporations over five decades — TWA, Texaco, Time Warner, Motorola, Apple, Dell, eBay, Xerox, and many more — pushing for management changes, buybacks, spinoffs, and sales. His approach is adversarial where necessary and has earned him both admiration and contempt on Wall Street. His holding company Icahn Enterprises trades publicly and gives investors direct exposure to his investment approach. In recent years he has faced significant challenges, including a critical short report by Hindenburg Research in 2023 that scrutinized IEP's valuation.
philosophy_quote: My investment philosophy, generally, with exceptions, is to buy something when no one wants it. That's how you get the best value.

notable_trades.title: TWA (1985–1988)
notable_trades.desc: Took over Trans World Airlines through a hostile acquisition, took it private, and extracted hundreds of millions before selling the airline.

notable_trades.title: Texaco (1988)
notable_trades.desc: Bought a major stake in Texaco during its bankruptcy and made over $500M as the company restructured and recovered.

notable_trades.title: Apple campaign (2013–2014)
notable_trades.desc: Pushed Tim Cook to dramatically accelerate Apple's share buyback program. Apple announced a massive capital return program shortly after.

notable_trades.title: Herbalife long (2013–2018)
notable_trades.desc: Took the opposite side of Ackman's famous short, going long Herbalife. Exited profitably, but not before a dramatic multi-year standoff.

notable_trades.title: Energy & industrial restructuring
notable_trades.desc: Icahn's portfolio continues to focus on undervalued companies with potential for operational improvement or corporate restructuring.

bio: Terry Smith is the UK's most prominent stock picker and is often called 'the British Warren Buffett.' After a distinguished career as a sell-side analyst and then CEO of Collins Stewart and Tullett Prebon, he founded Fundsmith in 2010 at age 57. The fund's simple three-part philosophy — buy good companies, don't overpay, do nothing — has resonated with hundreds of thousands of UK retail investors and made Fundsmith one of the largest equity funds in Europe by assets.

Smith is famous for his annual shareholder letters, which are candid, witty, and sharply critical of investment industry conventions he views as wasteful or misleading. He invests globally in high-quality consumer, healthcare, and technology companies with high returns on capital and genuine pricing power. He lives in Mauritius and has been openly critical of UK tax policy. His fund's long-term track record consistently places it among the top-performing large-cap equity funds globally.
philosophy_quote: Buy good companies. Don't overpay. Do nothing. It sounds simple because it is. The enemy of a good investment plan is the urge to do something.

notable_trades.title: Microsoft (long-term)
notable_trades.desc: One of Fundsmith's longest-held positions, bought at relatively modest valuations before the cloud transformation drove a decade of outperformance.

notable_trades.title: Meta Platforms
notable_trades.desc: Bought Meta during its 2022 trough when sentiment was extremely negative. The position has returned multiples since.

notable_trades.title: Philip Morris / IDEXX
notable_trades.desc: Fundsmith has long held consumer staples and healthcare companies with extraordinarily high returns on capital, generating compound returns over many years.

notable_trades.title: Twitter pre-acquisition
notable_trades.desc: Held Twitter before Elon Musk's acquisition, which provided an exit at a premium, though the position underperformed for years beforehand.

notable_trades.title: Consumer & healthcare compounders
notable_trades.desc: Fundsmith's core holdings remain high-quality consumer brands and healthcare companies with durable competitive advantages and pricing power.

bio: Robert Vinall is one of Europe's most respected independent fund managers, running RV Capital from Germany since 2008. After working at Deutsche Bank and then Berkshire Hathaway's investment team, he founded RV Capital with a small group of long-term oriented investors. The fund is notable for its extreme concentration — typically holding just 10–15 positions — and its willingness to hold companies for a decade or more. Vinall writes annual letters to his investors that are widely circulated and respected for their clarity and intellectual honesty.

RV Capital has delivered exceptional long-term returns with a portfolio that has evolved over the years from European value stocks toward a more global, quality-growth orientation. Vinall is deeply influenced by Buffett, Munger, and the Berkshire philosophy, but has developed his own distinct approach that emphasizes businesses with network effects and recurring revenue models. He is unusually transparent about his mistakes and thought process, which has made his annual letters required reading among value investing practitioners globally.
philosophy_quote: The goal is not to have a diversified portfolio of average businesses. The goal is to own a concentrated portfolio of exceptional businesses and hold them for a very long time.

notable_trades.title: Meta Platforms
notable_trades.desc: Built a large position in Meta during the 2022 selloff, recognizing the company's durable network effects and improving capital allocation under Zuckerberg.

notable_trades.title: Booking Holdings
notable_trades.desc: A long-term holding in the dominant online travel platform, which has delivered compound returns through its network effects and pricing power.

notable_trades.title: European value situations (early)
notable_trades.desc: Early RV Capital returns were driven by identifying undervalued European businesses trading well below intrinsic value in the post-GFC environment.

notable_trades.title: Various value traps
notable_trades.desc: Like many value investors, Vinall has written candidly about positions that appeared cheap but proved to be value traps due to industry disruption.

notable_trades.title: Quality tech & platforms
notable_trades.desc: RV Capital's concentrated portfolio holds global technology and platform businesses with durable network effects and high returns on capital.

bio: Mason Hawkins co-founded Southeastern Asset Management in 1975 and has spent nearly five decades building one of the most respected deep value investment firms in the United States. Southeastern manages the Longleaf Partners family of mutual funds as well as significant institutional capital. The firm's approach is built on identifying businesses trading at large discounts to their intrinsic value, where management teams have substantial insider ownership and act as genuine owner-operators.

Hawkins and his team are patient and willing to hold positions for many years as value is recognized. The firm applies a strict '60 cents on the dollar' rule — only investing when they believe they can buy a dollar of value for 60 cents or less. Southeastern has been a vocal advocate for shareholder rights and has engaged in several prominent activist situations where management teams were destroying value. The firm is known for its intense focus on management quality and its willingness to challenge underperforming executives publicly.
philosophy_quote: We will only invest when we can buy a business for 60 cents on the dollar of our appraised value, run by management we trust to act as true owners of the business alongside us.

notable_trades.title: FedEx (long-term)
notable_trades.desc: Southeastern has been a long-term FedEx shareholder, recognizing the durable competitive advantages of its global logistics network.

notable_trades.title: Chesapeake Energy activism
notable_trades.desc: Engaged in a long public campaign against Chesapeake's founder Aubrey McClendon over governance failures and excessive compensation.

notable_trades.title: Various spinoff situations
notable_trades.desc: Longleaf has a strong track record in corporate spinoffs and restructurings, where complexity creates pricing inefficiency.

notable_trades.title: Energy sector (2014–2016)
notable_trades.desc: Several energy positions were painful during the oil price collapse, as companies Southeastern viewed as undervalued fell further.

notable_trades.title: International value
notable_trades.desc: Longleaf's funds have expanded internationally, finding value in Asian and European markets where US investors are underexposed.

bio: The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Trust manages the endowment that funds the Gates Foundation — one of the largest private philanthropic organizations in history. Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft in 1975 and led it to become the world's most valuable company before stepping back from day-to-day operations. Today his public market portfolio is managed with a long-term orientation focused on companies aligned with the foundation's global health, agricultural, and development goals, as well as core blue-chip holdings.

The foundation's 13F filings reflect the Trust's public equity holdings, which are managed by Michael Larson through Cascade Investment. The portfolio is notable for its large concentration in Berkshire Hathaway — a reflection of Gates's long friendship and intellectual partnership with Warren Buffett. The trust also holds significant positions in waste management, agricultural chemicals, and consumer staples, sectors that align with the foundation's thematic priorities around global sustainability and health.
philosophy_quote: I choose a lazy person to do a hard job. Because a lazy person will find an easy way to do it. The same principle applies to investing — find the simplest path to the best long-term outcome.

notable_trades.title: Berkshire Hathaway (long-term)
notable_trades.desc: The Trust's largest holding and one of its best long-term performers, reflecting Gates's personal friendship with Buffett and conviction in Berkshire's model.

notable_trades.title: Waste Management (long-term)
notable_trades.desc: A core long-term holding that aligns with sustainability themes and has delivered consistent returns through pricing power and market dominance.

notable_trades.title: Canadian National Railway
notable_trades.desc: A long-term holding in the dominant Canadian railroad, which has compounded capital at high rates through pricing power and volume growth.

notable_trades.title: Caterpillar / agricultural stocks
notable_trades.desc: Holdings in industrial and agricultural companies reflect the foundation's thematic focus on global food security and infrastructure development.

notable_trades.title: Diversified blue chips
notable_trades.desc: The trust maintains a diversified portfolio of high-quality blue-chip companies across sectors that align with long-term secular growth themes.

bio: Nelson Peltz co-founded Trian Fund Management in 2005 with Ed Garden and Peter May, building on a long career in activist investing and corporate turnarounds. Peltz's approach distinguishes itself from most activist funds by emphasizing operational improvement over financial engineering — Trian takes large stakes in companies and then works collaboratively with management to improve margins, capital allocation, and strategy, often securing board seats to execute the agenda from the inside.

Trian's target companies are typically large, well-known consumer and industrial brands that Peltz believes are underperforming their potential due to cost bloat, poor capital allocation, or strategic drift. Notable campaigns have included Procter & Gamble, GE, Wendy's, Heinz, Mondelez, and Disney. The P&G campaign — in which Peltz waged a nearly two-year proxy fight before winning a board seat — became a landmark in activist investing history for its scale and persistence.
philosophy_quote: We are not financial engineers. We are operators. We take large stakes in great brands that are underperforming and work alongside management to unlock the value that is already there.

notable_trades.title: Heinz (2006–2013)
notable_trades.desc: Built a major stake and pushed for improvements. Heinz was eventually acquired by 3G Capital and Berkshire Hathaway at a significant premium.

notable_trades.title: Wendy's turnaround
notable_trades.desc: Trian acquired a large stake in Wendy's and drove an operational restructuring that significantly improved franchisee economics and brand positioning.

notable_trades.title: Procter & Gamble (2017–2019)
notable_trades.desc: Waged the largest proxy fight in history for a P&G board seat. Won by a razor-thin margin and contributed to significant margin improvements.

notable_trades.title: GE (2015–2018)
notable_trades.desc: Took a large GE stake expecting operational improvement. GE's deeper structural problems proved more intractable than anticipated and the position lost money.

notable_trades.title: Consumer staples / Disney
notable_trades.desc: Trian has maintained positions in consumer staples companies and waged a high-profile campaign at Disney over strategic direction.

bio: ValueAct Capital was founded in San Francisco in 2000 and has established itself as one of the most influential activist investors in technology and healthcare. Led by Mason Morfit, who succeeded founder Jeff Ubben as CEO, ValueAct takes a collaborative rather than adversarial approach to activism — seeking board representation and working quietly with management teams rather than waging noisy public campaigns. This approach has made ValueAct a trusted partner to many management teams and boards.

ValueAct typically holds 5–10 large positions and regularly secures board seats, which gives it an unusual level of insight and influence over portfolio companies. The fund has been an investor in companies including Microsoft, Seagate, Adobe, Rolls-Royce, and Willis Towers Watson. Jeff Ubben, who ran ValueAct from 2000 to 2020, later founded Inclusive Capital Partners with a focus on ESG-driven activist investing. Under Morfit, ValueAct has maintained its technology focus while expanding into European situations.
philosophy_quote: We look for great businesses at inflection points — where the underlying business is sound but strategy, capital allocation, or management execution has fallen behind the opportunity.

notable_trades.title: Microsoft (2013–2014)
notable_trades.desc: ValueAct acquired a large Microsoft stake and board representation, contributing to the strategic pivot under Satya Nadella that transformed the company.

notable_trades.title: Adobe Systems
notable_trades.desc: Held a long-term position in Adobe through its transformation to a subscription software model, generating exceptional returns.

notable_trades.title: Rolls-Royce (2021–2022)
notable_trades.desc: Took a large stake in Rolls-Royce during a period of pandemic-related stress, contributing to the turnaround under CEO Tufan Erginbilgic.

notable_trades.title: Seagate Technology
notable_trades.desc: A position in hard drive manufacturer Seagate was challenged by the ongoing shift to flash storage, making the competitive dynamics difficult.

notable_trades.title: Technology & industrial turnarounds
notable_trades.desc: ValueAct's concentrated portfolio continues to focus on technology companies and industrial businesses undergoing strategic or operational transformation.

bio: Polen Capital was founded in 1979 by Stanley Polen in Boca Raton, Florida and has grown into a significant institutional asset manager specializing in high-quality growth equity. The firm's flagship Focus Growth strategy has delivered exceptional long-term returns by concentrating in a small number of businesses with above-average earnings growth, high and sustainable returns on equity, and strong free cash flow generation. It is now led by CEO Stan Moss and a deep team of fundamental analysts.

Polen Capital's philosophy is rooted in owning compounding machines — businesses where the underlying economics allow them to reinvest capital at high rates of return for many years. The firm avoids businesses with high debt, cyclical earnings, or commoditized products. This approach has led to a portfolio concentrated in healthcare, technology, and consumer companies with dominant market positions. Polen has expanded its offering beyond large-cap growth to include international and emerging market strategies following the same quality-first principles.
philosophy_quote: We want to own businesses that don't need us to be right about the economy, interest rates, or the market. If the business keeps compounding at high rates, everything else takes care of itself.

notable_trades.title: Amazon (long-term)
notable_trades.desc: A core long-term holding recognized early for its durable competitive advantages and ability to reinvest in high-return growth opportunities across multiple verticals.

notable_trades.title: Alphabet / Google
notable_trades.desc: Long-term position in Alphabet, viewed as a dominant advertising and cloud computing platform with durable network effects and pricing power.

notable_trades.title: UnitedHealth Group
notable_trades.desc: Healthcare managed care has been a consistent source of quality compounders in Polen's portfolio, with UNH a long-term core position.

notable_trades.title: Facebook / Meta (2018–2019)
notable_trades.desc: Exited Meta after the Cambridge Analytica scandal raised governance concerns, missing the eventual recovery and return to growth.

notable_trades.title: Healthcare & technology leaders
notable_trades.desc: Polen's concentrated portfolio holds the highest-quality large-cap growth businesses in healthcare technology, software, and consumer internet.

role: Founded by Sarah Ketterer & Harry Hartford
bio: Causeway Capital Management was founded in 2001 by Sarah Ketterer and Harry Hartford after they left Hotchkis & Wiley. The Los Angeles-based firm specializes in international and global equity strategies, combining fundamental bottom-up analysis with quantitative risk management. Causeway was an early pioneer in using quantitative tools to enhance and discipline traditional value investing, developing systematic screens to identify undervalued international stocks while managing portfolio risk.

The firm manages a range of international equity strategies for institutional clients including pension funds, endowments, and sovereign wealth funds. Causeway's approach emphasizes stocks trading at discounts to intrinsic value in developed international markets, with a particular focus on European and Asian equities. Sarah Ketterer has been a prominent voice arguing that non-US equities have been persistently undervalued relative to their American counterparts, and that international diversification offers compelling risk-adjusted returns for long-term investors.
philosophy_quote: The best international opportunities are often found in high-quality businesses that are temporarily out of favor due to macroeconomic concerns specific to their home markets — concerns that the patient investor can look through.

notable_trades.title: European financial recovery (2012–2015)
notable_trades.desc: Causeway bought deeply discounted European financial stocks during the Eurozone crisis, generating strong returns as systemic risk receded and valuations normalized.

notable_trades.title: Japanese value stocks
notable_trades.desc: Early and persistent exposure to undervalued Japanese companies generated strong returns as corporate governance reform and shareholder activism gained momentum.

notable_trades.title: Emerging market industrials
notable_trades.desc: Selective exposure to industrial and infrastructure companies in emerging markets at discounted valuations has been a consistent source of alpha.

notable_trades.title: European value / energy
notable_trades.desc: Causeway's portfolios currently hold European energy, financial, and industrial companies trading at significant discounts to US equivalents.

notable_trades.title: Asian technology / industrials
notable_trades.desc: Select positions in Asian technology and industrial companies with strong competitive positions and improving capital allocation.

bio: John Rogers Jr. founded Ariel Investments in 1983 with $200,000 at age 24, making it one of the first Black-owned investment management firms in the United States. The Chicago-based firm, whose logo is a tortoise ('slow and steady wins the race'), specializes in patient, long-term value investing in small and mid-cap companies that are out of favor with Wall Street. Rogers is one of the longest-serving fund managers in the mutual fund industry and a pioneering figure in promoting diversity in finance.

Ariel's approach involves buying companies with strong competitive positions and capable management teams when they are temporarily misunderstood or ignored by the market — and then holding them for years as value is recognized. The firm is known for its focus on overlooked sectors like media, financial services, and specialty retail. Rogers is a close friend and longtime associate of both Barack Obama and Warren Buffett, and Ariel has been a vocal advocate for closing the racial wealth gap through broader investment in the capital markets.
philosophy_quote: We are patient investors. We buy carefully selected, undervalued companies and hold them until the rest of the world recognizes their worth. The tortoise always wins.

notable_trades.title: Viacom / media consolidation
notable_trades.desc: Ariel's exposure to traditional media companies generated significant returns through consolidation waves as the industry restructured.

notable_trades.title: Small-cap value cycles
notable_trades.desc: Ariel's patient approach to small and mid-cap value stocks has generated strong long-term returns through multiple market cycles since 1983.

notable_trades.title: Charles Schwab (long-term)
notable_trades.desc: A long-term holding in the dominant discount brokerage platform that has compounded capital at high rates through industry consolidation.

notable_trades.title: Traditional media disruption
notable_trades.desc: Some legacy media positions struggled as digital disruption accelerated, though Ariel often held through these periods waiting for asset value to be realized.

notable_trades.title: Financial services / media
notable_trades.desc: Ariel's portfolios remain concentrated in financial services, specialty media, and selected consumer companies trading below intrinsic value.

bio: Mairs & Power is one of the oldest independent investment managers in the United States, founded in St. Paul, Minnesota in 1931. The firm is known for its extraordinarily low portfolio turnover — often holding individual positions for a decade or more — and its emphasis on Midwest-headquartered companies that it knows particularly well due to geographic proximity. This regional knowledge edge, combined with patient fundamental analysis, has produced a strong long-term track record across economic cycles.

The firm manages the Mairs & Power Growth Fund, which is among the longest-running equity mutual funds in the country. Its investment philosophy centers on companies with durable competitive advantages, strong management teams, and the ability to compound capital over very long time horizons. Mairs & Power has historically been concentrated in healthcare, financial services, and industrial companies headquartered in the Upper Midwest, including names like 3M, US Bancorp, Ecolab, and Medtronic.
philosophy_quote: We invest for the long term. This means we look for companies that will be stronger in five to ten years than they are today, and we are willing to hold through short-term volatility to capture that long-term value.

notable_trades.title: Ecolab (multi-decade)
notable_trades.desc: A long-term core holding in the specialty chemicals and water treatment company, which has compounded at exceptional rates for decades.

notable_trades.title: US Bancorp (long-term)
notable_trades.desc: The Minneapolis-based bank has been a persistent holding, delivering consistent returns through its conservative management and regional market dominance.

notable_trades.title: Medtronic (long-term)
notable_trades.desc: A long-term position in the medical device giant headquartered in Dublin (originally Minneapolis), benefiting from global healthcare demand.

notable_trades.title: 3M (2018–2023)
notable_trades.desc: A longtime core holding that disappointed as 3M faced PFAS litigation and structural challenges in its business model.

notable_trades.title: Healthcare & industrial compounders
notable_trades.desc: Mairs & Power's portfolio continues to be anchored in high-quality healthcare and industrial companies with long-term competitive advantages.

bio: AKO Capital was founded in London in 2005 by Nicolai Tangen, a Norwegian investor who previously worked at Egerton Capital. The firm runs a concentrated long/short equity strategy focused on high-quality European and global businesses with strong competitive positions and superior management teams. AKO has been recognized as one of Europe's top-performing hedge funds, known for rigorous fundamental research and a strong emphasis on corporate governance and sustainability factors.

In 2020, Nicolai Tangen was appointed CEO of Norges Bank Investment Management — Norway's $1.7 trillion sovereign wealth fund — stepping back from AKO's day-to-day management. AKO has maintained its investment approach under the leadership of its remaining partners. The firm also runs a significant charitable initiative, the AKO Foundation, which funds arts and education projects in the UK and Norway. AKO's portfolio has historically been concentrated in high-quality consumer, technology, and healthcare businesses.
philosophy_quote: We look for companies that will be structurally bigger and better in five years than they are today — businesses with pricing power, recurring revenue, and management teams that think and act like long-term owners.

notable_trades.title: European quality compounders
notable_trades.desc: AKO's core long book in high-quality European consumer and healthcare businesses has generated strong long-term returns through the power of compound growth.

notable_trades.title: Technology platform shorts
notable_trades.desc: AKO's short book has generated alpha by identifying overvalued technology companies with deteriorating fundamentals or competitive positioning.

notable_trades.title: LVMH / luxury goods
notable_trades.desc: Long-term exposure to European luxury goods companies with exceptional pricing power and brand equity has been a consistent driver of returns.

notable_trades.title: Global quality growth
notable_trades.desc: AKO's long book continues to focus on high-quality global businesses with sustainable competitive advantages, superior management, and long growth runways.

notable_trades.title: Short book — challenged businesses
notable_trades.desc: The short portfolio targets businesses facing structural disruption, competitive deterioration, or financial engineering that obscures fundamental weakness.

role: Founded by Nick Train & Michael Lindsell
bio: Lindsell Train was co-founded in 2000 by Nick Train and Michael Lindsell, two veteran UK fund managers who share a deep conviction in the enduring power of great brands and franchise businesses. The firm manages a small number of concentrated strategies — both UK and global equity — with a philosophy of buying exceptional businesses and holding them almost indefinitely. Portfolio turnover is extraordinarily low, with the firm sometimes holding positions for 15–20 years.

Nick Train is one of the most distinctive voices in UK fund management, known for his passion for media, spirits, and consumer brand businesses. His global equity fund has held companies like Diageo, Nintendo, and London Stock Exchange for many years, believing these asset-light, brand-driven businesses compound capital at rates that justify premium valuations. The firm experienced a difficult period from 2021–2023 as its UK and global funds underperformed due to the fund's relatively limited exposure to energy and resources, but long-term track records remain strong.
philosophy_quote: We believe the most durable competitive advantages belong to companies with intangible assets — brands, licenses, and networks — that get stronger with age. We buy these businesses and get out of the way.

notable_trades.title: Diageo (multi-decade)
notable_trades.desc: One of Lindsell Train's oldest and largest positions, the premium spirits company has compounded capital at exceptional rates through pricing power and geographic expansion.

notable_trades.title: London Stock Exchange Group
notable_trades.desc: A long-term holding in the financial infrastructure company that has transformed through acquisitions into a global data and analytics business.

notable_trades.title: Nintendo
notable_trades.desc: Held Nintendo for many years recognizing the enduring value of its game franchises and intellectual property, well ahead of the Switch's commercial success.

notable_trades.title: Experian / Pearson
notable_trades.desc: Some positions in data and education businesses underperformed as the competitive landscape and regulatory environment evolved.

notable_trades.title: Premium consumer brands
notable_trades.desc: Lindsell Train's core holdings remain premium consumer and media brands with intangible competitive advantages that compound intrinsic value over decades.

bio: David Abrams founded Abrams Capital Management in 1999 after working as a research analyst at Seth Klarman's Baupost Group. He brought Baupost's deep value philosophy with him — a focus on margin of safety, patience, and willingness to hold cash when opportunities are scarce. Abrams Capital is one of the most secretive and successful hedge funds in the country, rarely appearing in the press and doing no marketing to investors. The fund has a long waitlist and has been largely closed to new capital for years.

Abrams's investment approach emphasizes identifying fundamentally sound businesses or assets that are trading at large discounts to intrinsic value, often due to complexity, temporary problems, or market neglect. The fund will hold significant cash positions when compelling opportunities are unavailable. Long holding periods of 5–10 years are common. Abrams has generated exceptional long-term returns with very low correlation to the broader market, making the fund highly sought after by endowments and family offices.
philosophy_quote: We look for situations where the facts are much better than the price suggests. Often the best opportunities are the ones where something has gone wrong and the market has overreacted.

notable_trades.title: Post-GFC distressed situations
notable_trades.desc: Like his mentor Klarman, Abrams aggressively bought distressed assets after 2008 at prices that proved to offer extraordinary margins of safety.

notable_trades.title: Liberty Media complex
notable_trades.desc: Abrams has navigated the complex Liberty Media tracking stock structure, identifying value hidden by corporate complexity.

notable_trades.title: Various spinoffs and restructurings
notable_trades.desc: Abrams has a strong track record in corporate actions where complexity or forced selling creates mispricing relative to intrinsic value.

notable_trades.title: Energy value plays
notable_trades.desc: Some energy sector value investments proved difficult as commodity price volatility and structural changes created persistent headwinds.

notable_trades.title: Concentrated value positions
notable_trades.desc: Abrams's small concentrated portfolio holds deeply researched value positions across sectors where the fund has strong conviction in intrinsic value.
